summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived overview of the American Revolutionary War (1775–1783), an 18th-century conflict between Great Britain and its Thirteen Colonies, which declared independence as the United States of America with France as an ally. It gives the war's dates, the Peace of Paris result and the territorial changes it produced. It also describes the Siege of Yorktown in 1781, where Lord Cornwallis surrendered after the Franco-American army besieged his forces.
one_line: Overview of the 1775–1783 American Revolutionary War, which ended with British recognition of American independence via the Peace of Paris.
key_facts: The American Revolutionary War lasted from April 19, 1775 to September 3, 1783.
The war's ratification took effect on May 12, 1784.
The war is also known as the American War of Independence.
The result of the war was an Allied victory, culminating in the Peace of Paris.
Great Britain ceded to the United States the area east of the Mississippi River and south of the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence River.
Great Britain ceded East Florida, West Florida, and Menorca to Spain.
Great Britain ceded Tobago and Senegal to France.
The Dutch Republic ceded Negapatnam to Great Britain.
The Franco-American army laid siege to Yorktown on September 28, 1781.
Cornwallis negotiated a surrender at Yorktown on October 17, 1781.
7,685 soldiers became prisoners of the Americans after the Yorktown surrender.
Six thousand troops under Clinton departed New York on the same day as the surrender, sailing to relieve Yorktown.
A British attempt to break out across the river at Gloucester Point failed when a storm hit.
Cornwallis abandoned his outer defenses, which American troops immediately occupied, hastening his defeat.
Great Britain retained Canada and Gibraltar after the war.
